verses.1: And the LORD said to Moses, “Say to Aaron, ‘Put your hand over the rivers, over the streams, over the pools, and over the wells that are in Egypt.’”
verses.2: And Aaron laid his hand on the borders of Egypt. Then the river Nile flowed over the land of Egypt.
verses.3: And the Horemets did just that. They carried the crosses onto the land of Egypt.
verses.4: And the Pharaoh called for Moses and Aaron. He said, “Go and speak to Jehovah. Remove those magicians from before me and from my people. I will send out the people to worship Jehovah.”
verses.5: And Moses said to Pharaoh, “May I be made great in my death. I will serve you and your people, and I will destroy those who are rebellious among you and your descendants. But only during the day will I do so.”
verses.6: And he said to Mahar, “Do as you say, so that you may know that there is no God like our Lord.”
verses.7: And the priests were removed from you, from your household, and from your servants and from your people. They were taken away only in the day when you were to be destroyed.
verses.8: Moses and Aaron went out from Pharaoh’s presence. Moses cried out to Jehovah about the things that the magicians had done to Pharaoh.
verses.9: And Jehovah did as Moses said. So the frogs died from within the houses, from the courtyards, and from the gardens.
verses.10: And they were gathered together, one by one. And the land became fertile again.
verses.11: And Pharaoh saw that the sky became dark and gloomy. He did not listen to what Jehovah said.
verses.12: And the LORD said to Moses, “Say to Aaron, ‘Take your staff and strike the ground. It shall become a pillar throughout all the land of Egypt.’”
verses.13: And they did so. Aaron stretched out his hand over the land, and all the dirt on the earth became clean. In every part of Egypt, every spot on the land became clean.
verses.14: And the Harthumim did as they were commanded, to bring out the idols. But they couldn’t do it. So, the idols remained with people and animals.
verses.15: And the priests said to Pharaoh, “It is God who is the one who rules. So Pharaoh’s heart became stronger, and he did not listen to them as Jehovah had commanded.”
verses.16: And the LORD said to Moses, “Stand before Pharaoh in the morning.” Then he appeared before Pharaoh and said, “Thus says the LORD: ‘Send out my people and let them serve me.’”
verses.17: For if you do not send my people away, then I will be their messenger among you, and among your servants and your people. I will fill the cities of Egypt with them; they will also fill the land they live on.
verses.18: And on that day, I destroyed the land of Goshen. My people were living there, but I made it impossible for them to remain there at night, so that they would know that I, Jehovah, am near to them.
verses.19: And I have placed peace between my people and your people. In the future, this will be a time of peace.
verses.20: And so did Yahweh. He brought about a great destruction in Pharaoh’s house, in his servants’ houses, and throughout all the land of Egypt. The land was destroyed because of this calamity.
verses.21: And Pharaoh called upon Moses and Aaron, and said to them, “Go and worship your gods on the land.”
verses.22: And Moses said, “It is not right to do so. For the suffering of Egypt has been brought before our God. Let us therefore offer thanks for the suffering of Egypt before His eyes, and let Him not deceive us.”
verses.23: In three days we will go into the desert, and we will worship the LORD our God, as He has commanded us.
verses.24: And Pharaoh said, “I will send you away, and you shall worship Yahweh your God at the sea. But do not go too far; do not go so far that you will not be able to return.”
verses.25: And Moses said, “Look, I will go away from your midst. I will go and plead with the LORD. Then, in the morning, Pharaoh’s people will be freed from his rule. But only after that will I send the people to worship the LORD.”
verses.26: And Moses went out from Pharaoh and pleaded with Yahweh.
verses.27: And Jehovah did as Moses said. He removed Pharaoh’s servants from their positions, and none of them remained behind.
verses.28: And Pharaoh’s heart was filled with joy at that time, and he did not send out the people.
